title: The Mayoral Tiebreaker
logline: A dead-heat municipal vote activates an obscure charter proviso granting office to whichever candidate deposits the station's heavy brass founding bell on the council dais first.

roles.description: A popular labour leader running on docking wage reforms; energetic, loud, and disorganized.
The cautious sitting habitat manager; obsessed with procedural propriety and determined to prevent a labour takeover.
A port authority security cutter charged with keeping the ballot transit corridors peaceful.
An unpressurized storage depot in an abandoned industrial ring where obsolete civic artifacts are mothballed.
The central civic chamber where municipal elections are certified and oaths administered.

public_situation: A municipal council election ends in a certified tie, prompting election arbiters to invoke an unamended 90-year-old charter rule requiring physical delivery of the founding bell.
private_truth: The founding bell was quietly sold off as scrap brass decades ago by an embezzling clerk; the crate in the vault holds lead ballast stamped with fake ceremonial seals.

beats.public_change: Electoral sirens sound across the concourse as officials declare a tie and announce the relic race.

missions.reason: The reformist hires an independent pilot to fly to the unpressurized relic vault and recover the founding bell crate before the manager's team arrives.
missions.private_fact: Her campaign ran out of credit hours ago and she is paying the pilot using dockworker collection tin coins.

beats.public_change: The incumbent administrator posts municipal guards outside the council airlocks to enforce luggage weight restrictions.

missions.reason: The administrator hires an outside pilot to deliver emergency counter-weights to balance the dais scales, attempting to stall the bell's certification.
missions.private_fact: He knows the original bell was pawned by his own predecessor and fears the public scandal more than losing the election.

beats.public_change: Technicians uncrate the relic at the dock, discovering it is merely a crate of painted lead ingots with an old ledger.

missions.reason: The reformist needs the pilot to scan the dais ceremonial podium to verify whether the acoustic sensors require the real bell or merely certified weight.
missions.private_fact: She considers displaying the fake publicly, even if it triggers riots that tear down the municipal charter entirely.

beats.public_change: The final midnight deadline approaches while the port patrol tightens a cordon around the council docking bay.

missions.reason: The reformist needs the pilot to run the security cordon so the delivery can reach the council dais before midnight.
missions.private_fact: The patrol commander hails mid-flight to offer the pilot a municipal immunity pardon if they dump the crate into the disposal chute instead.

player_choice.prompt: With the cordon cleared and the fake bell exposed, the pilot must choose what to present to the council tribunal.

options.label: Deposit the weighted crate on the dais to seat the reformist
Present the old ledger proving the bell was pawned

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot breaks the patrol and delivers the crate to the dais before midnight.
resolutions.summary: {role:reformist_candidate} is sworn into office on the weighted dais. {role:incumbent_administrator} yields, and dockworker wages increase across the station.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot delivered the tiebreaker relic past security guards, seating the union candidate.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot takes the patrol commander's pardon and dumps the crate.
resolutions.summary: The midnight deadline passes without delivery. {role:incumbent_administrator} declares the charter default and retains control under emergency bylaws.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot took a port pardon, letting the old manager retain power after an electoral tie.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot presents the pawn ledger proving the bell was stolen decades ago.
resolutions.summary: The pawn scandal erupts on the council floor. Both campaigns are discredited, the municipal charter is suspended, and outer investors freeze funding.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot exposed that the station's founding bell had been pawned for scrap, collapsing the government.

resolutions.summary: No bell arrives before the midnight chime. {role:incumbent_administrator} suspends the election and rules by municipal decree while strikes spread.

loose_threads.detail: The pawn receipt tucked in the relic ledger is countersigned by a liquidation brokerage that still holds commercial leases on the outer ring.
The serial numbers on the lead ingots match ballast weights removed from a municipal dredge tender during the previous decade's refit.

radio_hooks: Municipal electoral board deadlocked; 90-year-old bell race charter rule activated in {system}.
Supporters of rival candidates stage noisy vigils outside council chambers awaiting relic arrival.
Port authority denies claims that security patrols are blocking transit routes to the voting dais.

voice_direction.reformist_candidate: Boisterous, rapid-fire speech with frequent populist quips. Never admits she has not read the station municipal code.
voice_direction.incumbent_administrator: Dry, punctilious, and pauses frequently to consult procedural notes. Becomes shrill whenever the station vault is mentioned.
